decisions.statement: A page property stands in two trees.
This check holds the properties tree to the parts tree one page at a time.
Every page whose page type sits under `page-property` is judged.
A page type the change itself puts under `page-property` counts.
A record property declares its fields the same way a page type declares its properties.
A `one-of-property` page declares its members the same way a page type declares its properties.
The declarer of a page is one directory listed on the index as the change leaves the index.
A type that stops declaring a property leaves that property judged.
A page type the change takes away leaves the properties that page type declared judged.
Those properties are looked for in the withdrawn body rather than among the change's own pages.
Which page sits at a path is read from the body at that path.
An id the index files no page for is passed over rather than thrown on.
Why nothing is filed for an id is not said here.
A page stating no `id` is refused in words beside this check in every phase.
A body that will not load is refused in words beside this check in every phase.
A page property the change takes away is passed over.
That a declared property has a page is no business of this check.
`relation-resolves` refuses a declared property that has no page.
How many page types declare a property is not judged.
A property is declared by an address naming the page type that property is.

definition: the check refusing a page property that no page type declares
